reason: Ruby's `Regexp.escape` is a core-library call with no JS counterpart; each port spells the same escaping through a file-local helper (`regexpEscape`, `escapeRegExp`) or an inline character-class replace, so the call is made under a different name. Pre-existing divergence, newly VISIBLE to the gate: `escape` only entered the ported-call population when `ActiveSupport::FileUpdateChecker#escape` (file_update_checker.rb:146-148) was ported.

inflector/transliterate.rb:123 calls `transliterate(string, locale: locale)`, skipping the middle positional `replacement` (default "?"). TypeScript cannot omit a middle positional argument: passing `undefined` still records a 3-argument call, so every spelling diverges from the 2-argument Ruby site.
